To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the design of a content router is a challenging task that requires a careful analysis of the design space; 2) the design of the content router should be based on an architecture with a flexible forwarding table that can support different forwarding schemes; 3) the design of such an architecture is feasible; 4) a content router can be designed and implemented in a modular fashion; 5) a content router is feasible in terms of memory and processing resources; and 6) the

(i) a content router can be designed and evaluated in the form of a proof-of-concept implementation that runs on a commodity PC, (ii) the content router can support forwarding tables with hundreds of millions of prefixes, (iii) the content router achieves a forwarding rate of up to 10 Gbps, and (iv) the content router uses less than 10% of the available processing units in a high-speed router.

Caesar: 1. uses a novel content name lookup scheme that is based on a trie and is optimized to minimize the number of memory accesses, 2. is able to forward at high speed, and 3. is the first content router design that supports name-based high-speed forwarding.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(i) the design of a novel content forwarding algorithm that supports unlimited length content names, (ii) the design of the hardware architecture of a content router and (iii) the design and evaluation of a content router that uses a single ASIC to support forwarding tables with billions of prefixes.
the design of high-speed forwarding engines for content-based networking, which are able to handle the unprecedented size of forwarding tables that will be needed in the future.
the design of a content router that can forward billions of packets per second using content names with unlimited length.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the design and implementation of Caesar is a significant contribution to the ICN community.
we have designed and evaluated a content router that is capable of supporting a billion content prefixes, with unlimited characters, and forwarding at line rate.
Caesar is the first content router for high speed forwarding on content names, that is able to handle billions of content prefixes with unlimited length.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how to build a content router that can support the same forwarding throughput as current routers while using less than a third of their forwarding table size.

we have designed and built a prototype of a content router that is capable of forwarding packets at a line rate of 10 Gb/s, while using a forwarding table that has a billion content names and unlimited characters.
we have designed and implemented the first content router for high speed forwarding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of a content router for highspeed forwarding can be based on the design of an IP router, with a few key modifications to support name-based forwarding.
content routers do not need to be fundamentally different from today's IP routers, as the forwarding table size is the main bottleneck in the design of content routers.
, in contrast to traditional longest prefix match, name-based forwarding can be efficiently implemented in high-speed routers.
